items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: Mitch Miller followed by Elvis or the other way around.

ctx.x: We would get that occasionally but it was rare. It was rare for the clientele that we were playing for. I think we had a couple of rock & roll things that were, you know, popular, also the “Hucklebuck,” you know popular dance kind of things. But nothing really current for that period. I mean you have to remember that also in that period people were singing “Oh My Papa” and things like that were in parallel universe with the Elvis Presleys and the others.

That’s a terrific way to say that and I’ve been fascinated by that, because when you look at the top ten from a particular month and week in the mid-50s you see exactly that. Mitch Miller followed by Elvis or the other way around. It’s really fascinating.
Yeah. And you remember the Hit Parade of course, that would give you the top ten or top fifteen. Well Pop also bought these books. They were combo books called “Combo Orks.”
